plain: Special permission to be excused from a rule or law

webster.text: Distribution; the act of dealing out to different persons or places; as the dispensation of water indifferently to all parts of the earth.

more.text: The granting of a license, or the license itself, to do what is forbidden by laws or canons, or to omit something which is commanded; that is, the dispensing with a law or canon, or the exemption of a particular person from the obligation to comply with its injunctions.

That which is dispensed or bestowed; a system of principles and rites enjoined; as the Mosaic dispensation; the gospel dispensation; including, the former the Levitical law and rites; the latter the scheme of redemption by Christ.

example.quote: This is a duty from which nothing can give him a dispensation.
